_comment: Your engineering standards, as data. The document itself usually lives in a wiki and belongs to whoever owns architecture; this file is its machine-readable copy, so changing a standard is an edit here rather than a code change plus a deploy. The page reads `rules` to decide what applies to a repository of each type, and shows `source` under the heading so a reader can see which revision the figures were judged against. Bumping the rules here without bumping `source.version` is what the staleness warning on the page is meant to catch.
_rulesComment: One entry per Component-Inventory type (the `type-*` topic on the repository). A type with an empty object is deliberately OUT OF SCOPE rather than failing — say nothing about what your standards don't cover, or every library fails for having no database. Values are matched against the scanned value on WORD boundaries — 'Java' matches 'Java 21' but not 'JavaScript' — and ' / ' is a list of alternatives, so 'JavaScript / TypeScript' passes on either.

rules._LibraryComment: The Golden Path describes web applications and backend services. It says nothing about shared libraries, and says explicitly that what it does not describe is at the team's discretion — so a library carries no rules. Give Library its own rules the day the document grows a section about libraries.
